review_text: Probably in the ball park of about -1000 hours across all platforms. I've been playing 'World' on- and off now since around 2020, and have never considered the game to be bad. No matter how long my break is I always end up revisiting it for a couple of months at a time. I have beaten every monster, (excluding Safi, and Kulve*) solo; so as far as reviews go- the average solo player can look to me to get insight on what the experience will be like. I want to leave this review to really open up a gods-honest opinion, giving a good and bad part about every instance in the game. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- THE GRIND: Yes, monster hunter is grindy. You should absolutely not expect to play this game without sinking upwards of 50+ hours in farming- and gear grinding. In reality, that estimate is probably much larger depending on a variety of variables. The game has tedious mechanics at times- and can definitely impact a long time playthrough without breaks, which could lead to burnout. This grind only exponentially grows throughout the game, as the base game is generally much more manage-able than the DLC. With this being said, the grind is absolutely not as demoralizing as one might expect. As far as I was concerned, I still had tons of fun farming, and sometimes- although arduous the feeling of finally getting a rare drop or finally crafting a piece of gear more than made up for the time spent getting it. You can really dump hours upon hours into creating your own builds, and experimenting with different weapons. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ARTWORK: The monsters- and characters are some of the most memorable things in the game for me. I love the artwork and design of the creatures you fight in this game, and how they embed themselves into the environment. The immersion comes from the danger, and that some monsters are outright- terrifying to come across. The nature, and geography of the locations you traverse through are also gorgeous, and have proper- depth and design. A lot of the creatures develop their powers from the locale which they are most commonly found- which helps again to build on that immersion. The design of the armor is honestly a 50/50. Some sets have stunning looks, while others can look really funny. There is no shortage of "fashion" or designs out there, so the possibility of customizing your character is really endless when it comes to color, monster parts, or themes. In-fact, a substantial amount of my playtime was also spent getting vanity gear, which includes cosmetics to drip out my character. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- COMMUNITY: Don't reference your experience to isolationists who villainize the game by targeting people who don't use their weapon. The monster hunter experience is wonderful, and is intended to be played as you see fit. Although there are definitely do's and don'ts in multiplayer, id say probably around 90% of the player-base are genuinely helpful, kind players. I love this, as coming from previous games It felt as if the community for monster hunter was a really welcoming experience when I started out. There are some utterly jaw-dropping clips, and speed runs out there. The talent of the community and the competition between fastest-speed runs never ceased to amaze me as an average player. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- DIFFICULTY: There is some stigma out there- that confuses difficulty for annoyance. Some monsters in this game are annoying to fight, with gimmicky mechanics. That is not the same as difficult monsters. Besides the obvious endgame challenges- there really aren't too many monsters that the average player couldn't beat or would have trouble fighting. Hell, even Fatalis- which took me about a month of planning fell eventually, which was done multiple times with un-optimal builds and countless mistakes. Everything can be learned, and no one should be deterred by a monster just because it seems difficult. This game is really not too challenging, and for the most part, the average monster will at-most, just keep you on your toes rather than require you to completely focus on it. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- STORY: I'm going to be honest. The story in monster hunter is really nothing to go all crazy about. The characters lack depth, and have corny- random lines. The beauty in the story doesn't really come from the acting or narrative, but rather the climax. Most end-fights or fights that are big canonical moments make up for little filler monsters. For example, I really enjoyed Valkanas's ark, as well as the Shara-Ishvalda story, regardless of how their fights were. The characters do have interactions with each other but they seem quite dull, and lifeless at times. To be quite frank, the story is also really not what we want out of the game- as we more than make up for its qualities with strong combat and mechanics. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 100% TROPHY: So that just about covers it- community, experience, and game design. The last thing I wanted to touch upon is something that I myself have been apt to. There are many, people out there who consider themselves completionists. This game, naturally- comes along with a set of 100 achievements which can be completed throughout the story and the side-quests. My honest- truth is that if your are thinking about going for the platinum trophy on monster hunter-DONT. I am not even going to get started on the implications of some of these achievements, but the only thing that anyone needs to know is that a general sum of the achievements are solely reliant on RNG. RNG numbers in-fact- that are not common in the slightest. I want to make it clear that a 100% trophy in this game will come up to 600 or more hours of playtime for the average player- especially if your playing solo. I am currently at the 500 hour mark on my character, (which i started in December of 2024), and have just-now, gotten to the "endgame" achievements AKA crown hunting. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I am personally planning on completing world in the foreseeable future, getting my platinum and getting the hell out of dodge. My experience with this game has lasted me through some of the most memorable moments in my life, and because of it this game belongs to a special area in my heart. I know that deep down, I will always admire it- but I would love to move on to 'Wilds' at some point. So for those who have played 'Wilds' - and want to check out other monster hunter experiences, try World. The UI and initial loop of the game can be confusing for brand new players but in the long run- I expect that there are more than a few who might enjoy this game as much as I have for the last six years of my life.

Elden Ring is bellow average overrated overhyped mediocrity that didn’t deserve GOTY 3.5/10 1. STORY 3/10 Has interesting lore if you watch youtube videos but that is expected to be extra and not something you are obligated to do to understand the story, the story in game is for most part absent… that alone disqualifies the game from 10/10 even if everything else was perfect (everything else is indeed not perfect, actually not even close to 10), even when environmental story telling is used as an excuse, it still does very poor job at it, dark fantasy on its own doesn’t work once its removed from high fantasy setting where usually its just a small part of much bigger world… lord of the rings works because you can see the contrast… when you make the entire world look bleak it doesn’t make you feel anything anymore, and no it has nothing to do with morally ambiguous characters, i prefer those actually, what i don’t like is expecting me to feel something about a world that looks exactly the same… speaking of world 2. WORLD 2/10 Just straight up a chore, want to reach that lake? To bad you can’t glide so you have to go all the way around, fall in a ditch? To bad you can’t climb so you have to go all the way around… want to negate fall damage with the horse double jump? to bad you can’t… like im a missing something here or fromsoft still hasn’t discovered the most core mechanic of double jump… i get that jumping is alien tech to this guys so i guess that explains why it feels so bad, they copied the entire world from breath of the wild but didn’t bother copying the core traversal tools necessary to make the world enjoyable to traverse… other things such as all biomes just morphing into one made me lose complete track of time, everything looks the same (DLSS 5 is not the reason for that) there are so many reused enemies, assets and dungeons that doing any form of side content is not worth it… like its so bad that the map feels procedurally generated but somehow it was hand made? The world is nowhere near as big as people made it to be… pick a farm, milk it until you get as many runes as physically fast as possible for the shortest possible time and min max your character so you can finally do the “campaign” this is literally the entire progression system of the game, speaking of progression 3. PROGRESSION 0/10 Actually horrible, just straight up unplayable without external guide, going blind here would’ve made me uninstall and refund the game…. I never follow build guides for games and beat all the pinnacle bosses in poe 2 and not even once followed a build guides… but here its mandatory to even play the game… NPCs say bunch of nonsense… rarely if ever explain things and for most part ignored them or didn’t even find them… No quest side window or markers means you have no idea what you are supposed to do, world and NPCs don’t make it any easier either… Loot feels horrible which makes no sense for an ARPG, like thats literally the whole point of an ARPG… the loot… how do you screw this bad to the point that the only way to progress is to follow build guides and have to look the individual weapons, items and gear on a website map to find them… no side content such as cave or fortress felt rewarding… (all who were reused assets of course) 4. UI/UX, CONTROLS, CAMERA 0/10 My gosh, the most horrific controls i have ever endured… probably second worse after crimson desert (Thank god didn’t buy that steaming pile of trash) everything is wanky and weird and the UI is atrocious… like there is no way there is no key for inventory… thats straight up disrespectful towards the player… it costs the devs nothing to do that and somehow its missing from the game… game is locked at 60fps and has no DLSS SR forcing me to use mods and also no mini-map, seriously? It doesn’t make the game more realistic or quirky… its annoying af, the whole UI is convoluted and just straight up horrible… even compared to old games its terrible… you know what else is terrible? Camera… can’t imagine that camera with all the AoE garbage in the DLC, good thing is i don’t even plan to find out (even tho i did bought the DLC) 5. GRAPHICS 4/10 They are fine, but they are not as good as people make them, the lighting and skybox is over compensating for the otherwise bellow average mediocre graphics and man there are moments where the textures are so bad it looks like a ps3 game… its so bad that even DLSS 5 doesn’t know what to do with it so it turns it into a giant blob of liquid noise unlike anything I’ve seen before, sure could be a mod problem but toggling it off absolutely showed horrible textures in that spot that don’t match the resolution of the tiles or bricks nearby… creating inconsistent resolutions in the same room… the render distance is bad and the texture quality completely deteriorates on distance the moment you look in any view of the world that wasn’t intended to be used as advertising material (such as limgrave door view) 6. MUSIC 3/10 Aside from the limgrave one, main theme, tree sentinels one and malenia’s song, everything is boring, mid and forgettable… genuinely disappointing music… 7. PLATFORMING -10000/10 don’t ever include platforming section in your games ever again 8. DUNGEONS 2/10 Repetitive, boring and short… same layout for most part… same style, same material… everything just blurs together, the difficulty of the game is extensively used to make the cleaning of this areas far slower to dilute the actual size and length of the dungeons (just like the rest of the game)… there a few that stand out like Stormveil Castle that are medium size but still tiny compared to Zelda standards… overall the dungeons are extremely disappointing and often the way the developers have designed the levels feels like they are making it on purpose unclear so you miss out on “big things”… 9. DIALOGUE, VOICE-LINES, BEHAVIOUR 3/10 I get that Japanese games always have goofy and corny voice lines in their games but elden ring setting and tone is supposed to be serious yet the moment a boss says something its always some non sensical goofy garbage, while the NPCs having those type of lines is sometimes fine, the bosses completely ruin the tone of the game, fromsoft has failed at the first step of making bosses if a boss doesn’t feel scary… and no its appearance is less then 10% of what makes a boss scary, its behaviour and how they speak as well as their ambition is the primarily factor… it feels like fromsoft doesn’t know what it wants elden ring to be, do you want the world to feel cruel and unjust? Then why no encounter ever feels personal? 10. CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP 0/10 Boring, repetitive and unfun, there is no point of killing any of the enemies because they will just respawn every time you go on a bonfire leading to feeling like you are not doing any form of progress, why bother with them if you can optimise for specific farm and only do that instead? And for the items you need you will just follow build guide so you know where to go and how to get what you need… bosses are same story… keep repeating the same thing over and over again until you finally beat it or over level your self so much that you demolish it… no fun middle ground… everything feels like artificial way of increasing the playtime and length of the game. The game has nothing other then difficulty to offer did git gud and beat malenia but to bad the game never got better, tried to like the game but its just not a good game and I don’t think i will be playing anymore (unless i use mods that very heavily alter the gameplay), fromsoft has failed to modernise and keep up with modern standards and thats even more apparent with Nightreign… a game that had massive potential. Also i-frames suck and is the reason why bosses have obnoxious long attack combos as form of corny punishment… no idea what fire giant is and have zero intentions on finding out Also horse armour DLC, you serious?

Never thought I'd really enjoy a roguelike as much as I dig Darkest Dungeon at this point. The story is simple and blunt, your goal given right on without too much context about everything. And given the focus of the game is the gameplay and about dungeon exploring, this is perfectly fine. The graphics and music has a dark atmosphere in general, enhancing the setting and giving it the right vibes for the gloomy and dark situations you're getting thrown in. The art style has its nice and recognizable way to make the trips into the dungeons and explore those a good experience overall. Given the genre, it's a repetitive cycle of you preparing your characters for the next exploration trip, expand your options in town to make them stronger, make services cheaper, and giving you better odds at not running into misery. Many classes to pick and build your teams around, themed teams for specific dungeon types making things a bit easier within those. Given the amount of skills every class has, you can go with different approaches and builds for them, not being a one-way ticket to only get used as a tank but a tank also able to go into an offensive build if you like this approach more. Dungeon exploration is a matter how many items you took with you and into what obstacles you'll run eventually. Dungeon designs randomized, some dungeons ending up with a more tedious room layout, some on the straight and simple progression. Resource management will decide how decent or not a trip will be, gathering items to sell or collect for town upgrades, making decisions what to keep and what to drop as the inventory isn't the biggest. Quest tasks vary from exploring the whole dungeon to find specific objects to interact or to collect, different sizes and difficulties for the dungeons existing. Battles are in general RPG style, choosing the skills you want to use, having specific ranges or positions you have to be in to use those. Hit and dodge chances giving everything an RNG touch while turn order also not solely relying on one stat but also has some RNG to it included. Enemy variation is big enough to not feel like you run into the same enemies over and over while different areas have a focus on specific enemy types. Your characters will get stressed and once too stressed, things could go 180 and make a run more complicated. With how much RNG is included within passives, status effects, and many more, the runs you expect to be easy may still turn something into results not expected, making it fun despite you doing these runs constantly. Difficulty for the game is to me in the mid-levels, some enemies being on the comfier side to deal with while some will give you some headaches. Bosses do something annoying and even nasty, learning about those things when encountering those. And given a character's death is permanent, you have to make the right decisions whether to continue or be safe and bail out of a dungeon before worse happens. The game plays a lot of mind games with you and your decisions, but I didn't feel anything was overly difficult to even unfair. You can adapt to situations and areas with the right setups so things will get easier if you know what you do. What increased my experience by a lot is how much the modding scene has to offer for the game. I only knew a few skins for classes to exist which were the reason why I got mildly interested in DD in the beginning, but once I saw what options I have and what modders created over the last decade, I've found a lot of visual changes which made the game a feast for my eyes. New classes, skins for those, many ways to tweak your game and experience it with a new touch. Not to mention that you can tweak a few things by yourself rather easy once figuring out which files are for what. I've made a few changes to my NPCs myself, and will surely do more of that in the future. Negatives about the game? The usual easy to learn, and hard to master mentality comes into play for sure. It took some hours to get a gist of how to operate my runs, what options I have to make them a bit comfier, and what can wreck you and what to look out for. I personally felt that the passives you may get after a successful run more often than not went into the negatives, receiving more bad passives over good ones, but there's eventually a mod to balance that out a bit more. Not sure if it's intended like that but felt a bit more geared towards receiving some bad passives, but could just be me not having the best luck with those. Expect to curse a lot when your 90%+ hit chances end up in missing enemies, or you getting smacked into dangerous levels out of nowhere which can be funny in a grim way~ I'm usually not much into roguelikes, but the combination of how I can tweak the game to my liking plus the bit I've seen and knew about the game got me into giving it a try. Which resulted in my little issue to pick from a very few roguelikes to play whenever time and mood allows it to now being settled into these dungeons. To me, there's no real finish to the game, a lot of things you can do and also add with the help of mods to have a reason to come back whenever you desire. And when on sale, it's just a few bucks which is a lot you get out for such little investment. I like my games with clear goals and beating them, but this game is now fully accepted by me to come back to and enjoy the game.

tl;dr: great game, but with a dev team so capricious it made me miss WoW. Warframe is a really fun game, with incredible gunplay, movement, and an in-depth building system that proves addicting. In fact, I'll likely return and update this review if it improves! With that being said, Warframe, as it stands, is fundamentally held back by how its devs choose to handle multiple aspects of it. This includes things like: Adding Actual Organized Group Content for the first time in years, BUT still actively refusing to add a group finder system, forcing you to use an archaic recruit chat system. Compounding this, Icebind, while incredibly fun and one of the highlights of the game right now, is partially reliant on having teammates that know basic mechanics. The baseline difficulty of the game does not prepare the average player to know what a "mechanic" is, leading to a lot of friction when combined with the group-making system that became obsolete in the late 2000s. Many things in the game reward organized and efficient group play (See: Radshares, Arbitrations, Arena nodes), but not having a large dedicated friend group means you're going to have a really bad time actually doing any of it with how fast the recruitment chat moves. Really bad time-gating, with most forms of gearing up being locked behind weeklies (Archon Hunts, Icebind, Netracells, ETA, EDA, just to name a few). I can't blame them for this- as weeklies are the best way of getting player retention. However, the current Incarnon Genesis system is obnoxious, taking [b] NINE WEEKS [/b] to fully cycle, getting longer with each new update to the system. Combine this with how Digital Extremes often uses Incarnons as a band-aid fix for underperforming/old weapons, and each new week makes getting the Incarnon you're chasing more and more annoying? Miss a week? Too bad, have fun waiting another several months for it to come back! In addition, there's a lot of grinds in content islands that end up taking tens of hours of time-gating and grinding for... Not much apart from the very specific thing you want for your build. Warframe really doesn't respect your time, and it knows this. Warframe as a whole has terrible QoL, especially before the "endgame." Crafting times take upwards of 3 1/2 days for a new frame, not including the grind itself. A particular gripe of mine is how cumbersome the HUD can be sometimes, with no way to tell what the tens of buff and debuffs that pop up mid-fight are apart from the very short, missable text that appears when it first triggers- and even then, you don't know what it does without looking it up afterwards. The trading system, while made palatable by a third party website, shows a troubling side of Digital Extremes that seemingly expects its playerbase to do the heavy lifting in making its incredibly archaic systems work through use of third-party websites, Discord servers, and Wikis. Worst of all and the primary reason I've left, is Digital Extremes' utterly baffling kneejerk-heavy balancing philosophy. They have an incredibly bad history of nerfing anything that's not what they [i] want [/i] to be meta into the ground, leading to an incredibly stale buildcrafting experience that's been solved since 2019. This leads to a hostile relationship with the game's own playerbase when combined with the game's premium currency, where people who spend money on builds feel as if they've been rugpulled when they get nerfed out of nowhere. A telling example of this was quite recently, with how Icebind and its primary reward, Riven Splicing, was rolled out. A few weeks after Riven Splicing was released, one of the traits only attainable by Riven Splicing was target nerfed, with a comedically low compensation given out. This pattern of whack-a-mole style nerfs effectively deleting anything that outperforms their precious Incarnon weapons, combined with making a proper build in a manner that doesn't involve weeks of grinding often requiring real money, has slowly turned the playerbase against each other. Especially with the recent Acid Shells nerf, I've seen people turn on each other and threaten to try and get each other's playstyles nerfed to keep their own safe for a little longer. This has slowly made the community more aggressive and gatekeeping over the past few years, sometimes even harassing content creators who make videos on their builds. While harassment is obviously never justified, can you really blame players for becoming more guarded about their builds? After all, the build you spent real money on can't be nerfed if you spend [i] more [/i] money to hide your weapon names and further conceal its true identity behind a skin, right? While I don't particularly dislike Warframe nor its developers, I can't ignore that the past year has been incredibly disappointing to play- and the game still feels like it has a complete lack of direction after over a decade, with nothing but underwhelming content island updates to show for it. I still have hope, as Icebind could be a great stepping stone to a future of actual endgame content! Unfortunately, I can't give a positive review for incomplete work that's been stringing me along for years. If you're planning on playing this, give it a bit, because it's not worth it in its current state.

(This review contains minor mechanical spoilers, and mentions minor details about the sequel at the end) Hades is one of the few games I always enjoy returning to, even after having completed the full story several times. The incredible attention to detail and unique style present in every aspect of the game have always impressed me, from the first time I played. The story is extremely well-written, immersive, and impactful. I was hooked to it and eager to progress it all the way through, and have started up a new save file to experience it again several times over the years. Progress feels meaningful and personal. More than any other game I have played, the world feels developed and alive. Characters have depth and respond to the things the player does, sometimes in the funniest and most unexpected ways. After over 200 hours of gameplay, I still encounter dialogues I haven't seen before. I greatly enjoy the combat system. It's simple but also has a high ceiling to develop your skill, and there is lots of room for personal preference. There are many mechanics which exist to provide variety to the builds you can make and incentives for exploring that variety, but also freedom to play the way you want to. There is room to choose how difficult you want the game to be— whether more casual to experience the story, or more challenging to push your limits. Players who enjoy challenges can utilize some optional mechanics that increase the difficulty in creative ways which push you to make use of everything you can, and be rewarded for doing so. Unlike many games, it's not just artificial difficulty either, there is genuinely unique content to enjoy in doing so (i.e. not just numbers going up, which is part of it, but also interesting twists and enemies gaining new attacks & abilities). There is also SO much content and replayability. Outside of the main story, there are so many other things you can choose to explore and progress, including side storylines, customizations, challenges, additional worldbuilding, and more. It doesn't feel like a chore, either— you can work on many things at once by just playing the game. Completionists can have a field day trying to max everything out if they so please. And, since the dungeons are randomized and there are so many build choices, no two runs feel the same. You are compelled to improve your adaptability and be ready for anything. At the same time, I would say the RNG is well-balanced, and there are systems you can unlock to greatly mitigate build-based RNG once you start finding ones you like to go for. Overall, I would say Hades deserves all the awards and nominations it's received and more, and I can easily recommend it to a variety of players. You can tell the developers put the utmost of their efforts and passion into making it. I love the art style and original music so much I've used screenshots as my desktop background and listen to the music outside of the game. With Hades 2 out now, there's even more to look forward to afterwards. I would highly recommend playing the original first, as while Hades 2 has its own story, it builds on the story from the first game and has lots of fun references.
